the_methodological_lesson.what: the same species of error occurred in two adjacent generations
the_methodological_lesson.detail: r3's carrier cited a verification that no longer reproduced (F-REV-R3-02); r4's record turned a 19-probe result into a general claim (F-REV-R4-06). Different shapes, same species: the record claims more than the measurement supports.
the_methodological_lesson.generalisation: a conclusion sentence must carry its measurement set inside the sentence. Write 'on the N probes this section reports, only C10 remains' rather than 'only C10 remains'. The difference costs nothing at write time and is unrecoverable at read time -- the next reader takes the latter as a universal proposition, and both author and reader believe they are the same sentence.
the_methodological_lesson.a_second_lesson: fixing the branch that was pointed at is not the same as closing the family. r4 closed the non-letter branch while '?' -- also a non-tchar character -- kept leaking; both are the same family ('the token class does not match'), and only one branch was registered. When the fix is 'widen a class', the boundary of the family is where the class ends, so the class's COMPLEMENT must be swept too -- and per position, because the same class has different reachability at the scheme position, the value position and the after-break position.
